question: Can TOPA remove the browser-only video-access blocker by reusing JANUS Retina/Telegram vision principles without importing Telegram transport or weakening K1 provenance requirements?

retina.intentional_change: TOPA preserves raw media and derived frames instead of deleting them after analysis because hunt reproducibility requires an auditable evidence trail.

telegram_vision.note: The recovered JANUS materials establish Retina image analysis and Telegram media/vision architecture, but not a source-complete historical handle_janus_video implementation. TOPA therefore implements a new transport-agnostic video bridge from those verified contracts instead of inventing missing legacy code.

requested: segment manifest and missing/corrupt segment information
camera timestamp basis/timezone and clock synchronization/drift
exact camera coordinates, identifiers, orientation and field of view
third remote/test camera status, location, surveyed baseline and FOV overlap

compact_result: The perception/tooling blocker is no longer represented as a generic inability to view video. TOPA now has a native evidence-preserving bridge from local/HTTP/public Drive media to hashes, metadata, deterministic frames, contact sheets and optional Retina inspection. What remains open is the scientific dataset boundary: identifying exactly which files constitute one complete blind raw day and freezing their camera/time/calibration metadata before K1 execution.
